title: Orsen and the Crown Anew
premise: In the city of Vellharrow, where magic was outlawed after the Sundering, Tamsin Ravensworth survives by selling harmless charms while hiding their gift for speaking with beasts. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, Tamsin is dragged into a conspiracy led by Orsen, a disgraced royal warden who once executed mages—including, unknowingly, Tamsin's mother. Together they must journey to the dying dragon-fires that anchor both realms and reforge the broken covenant between humans and dragons, even as Orsen's loyalty to the crown demands he arrest the very person he has come to love. In the end, Tamsin speaks the covenant anew at terrible personal cost—giving up their voice to the dragons—and Orsen chooses truth over duty, ruling beside a silent queen of beasts until the stars return.
about_author: Gideon Quintana is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent a decade listening to animals before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about outsiders who find family in unexpected places, from a cabin in the northern woods.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Selling charms in Vellharrow's night market, Tamsin quietly soothes a terrified cart-horse whose words warn of 'the sky going dark.' At midnight, every star vanishes and the border wards shatter like glass. Emotional beat: dread and denial—the life Tamsin built on invisibility cracks open in a single breath.

chapters.title: A Warden's Debt
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Royal Warden Orsen Hale investigates the fallen wards and finds dragon-scale residue—a magic only the old covenant could produce. His superiors order him to hunt the 'beast-speaker' rumored in the low quarter. Emotional beat: cold duty masking guilt over the mage executions he once carried out without question.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Hunted through the sewers by crown soldiers, Tamsin bargains with the rats for escape routes and learns the city's foundations are threaded with dead dragon-bones—the source of all ward-magic. Emotional beat: reluctant courage; Tamsin realizes their gift is the only map to saving the realm.

chapters.title: An Arrest That Isn't
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Orsen corners Tamsin in an abandoned temple but recognizes the mother's sigil on their charm-bracelet—the woman he executed three years ago. Instead of arresting them, he lies to his captain. Emotional beat: shame curdling into resolve; the first fracture in his loyalty to the crown.

chapters.title: The Road Under Ashen Skies
chapters.summary: POV: Alternating. Fugitives together, Tamsin and Orsen travel toward Mount Cinderfall, the last burning dragon-fire. Beasts along the road speak of a 'Hollow King' who ate the stars. Emotional beat: wary partnership warming into trust, punctuated by Tamsin teaching Orsen to hear what he'd been trained to kill.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Captured by the Hollow King's starless court—exiled mages who blame the covenant itself—they learn the truth: the crown broke the pact first, feeding dragon-fire to its wards for a century. Emotional beat: fury and grief; Tamsin's enemy and savior blur into one corrupt throne.

chapters.title: Where Loyalty Burns
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Rescuing Tamsin means betraying the crown openly; Orsen burns his warden's oath and fights his former brothers-in-arms. The Hollow King offers him a new crown if he hands over the beast-speaker. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal—Orsen chooses Tamsin and loses everything else.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: POV: Alternating. They reach Mount Cinderfall to find one ancient dragon, Ember-that-Was, barely alive, her fire nearly out. She will reforge the covenant only with a speaker willing to give their voice to the dragons forever. Emotional beat: quiet terror and tenderness; Tamsin and Orsen confess love knowing the price.

chapters.title: Covenant Anew
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. As the Hollow King's army storms the mountain, Tamsin sings the old words in every beast-tongue at once, pouring their voice into the flame. Dragon-fire roars back across the land; the stars reignite; the king turns to ash and hollow wind. Emotional beat: triumphant sacrifice—Tamsin saves two realms and loses their own song.

chapters.title: The Queen Who Listens
chapters.summary: POV: Orsen. Months later, Orsen serves as regent of a reformed realm while mute Tamsin governs the renewed covenant, speaking through dragons and sign. On the first anniversary, a single star flares and Tamsin hears—or perhaps imagines—one word in their mind: home. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging; love remade in a new language.
